summary: The checked-out and current upstream implementations still call ncclCommWindowRegister synchronously without a timeout, but the reported multi-rank NVIDIA NCCL deadlock cannot execute on the assigned single AMD gfx950 ROCm environment. No unvalidated behavioral fix was made.

tests.what_was_measured: PyTorch runtime identity and an actual elementwise GPU result on the assigned gfx950; CUDA is absent and HIP is 7.2.
The issue-specific synchronous registration and global reset paths remain in the recorded base.
The allocator file at current upstream main was byte-identical to the prepared base during investigation.

gpu_execution.evidence: probe_gpu.py executed tensor arithmetic on AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950. This only validates the assigned GPU/runtime and is not a reproduction of CUDA/NCCL symmetric registration.

remaining_limitations: Only one AMD gfx950 GPU was assigned; the issue requires multi-rank NVIDIA CUDA/NCCL execution.
ROCm PyTorch reports torch.version.cuda as null and cannot execute the embedded CUDA/NCCL allocator path.
NCCL 2.29.7, B200 hardware, GLM-5.3-Flash weights, and the reported TP4/EP4 traffic fixture were unavailable.
No timeout, logging-only, pre-sizing, or registration-coordination candidate was presented as fixed without affected-platform validation.
